questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There wer very many interesting subjects to choose from at the particular University and it has a good reputation especially within theoretical chemistry.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: THe academic pace was high

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly very easy. There was no welcome day for exchange students in chemistry, which was a bit weird, but they made documents with the most important things to remember.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not alot. There was one introduction day for all exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Maybe an introduction from other students, so thatyou would get to meet students would be nice since you really had to be very proactive about that yourself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was fairly close and public transportation is very good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dorm Meierwiessenstrasse is okay. The kitchen is horrible but the rooms and toilets were okay. The rooms are definetely not sound proof. Only exchange students live there, and it is quite cosy.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, you are guided through most steps. Just be aware that some mails can be blocked by your mail, and for houseing the deadline for acceptin/declining is very short.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They describe everything neede in mails, online Zoom meetings, documents, etc. So very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can call the exchange coordinater at your institute.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classses that I wanted. You can also chose master subjects. You can change them within I think the first week or so. Be aware that the schedule can change before the semester so check for overlaps.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check prerequisites for courses thoroughly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: THe academic level is high. everything is very organized and the teachers are very motivated, but it is VERY much self study. So find a study group.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The leve was high but not impossible. There is a lot to learn by heart, but the exams were not as difficult as excpected (unless you strive for very high grades) My impression was that it is very difficult to get above 5.5.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more individualized. There is not literature given in the same way but mainly book/article suggestions. The pace of the lectures is much higher, and there is not a lot of time for questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Classical simulations of biomolecules
Advanced quantum chemistry
Organometallic homogeneous catalysis
Algorithms and programming for chemistry
Electrochemistry: Fundamentals, cells and applications

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Classical simulations of biomolecules
Advanced quantum chemistry
Organometallic homogeneous catalysis
Algorithms and programming for chemistry

They were all specialized and very interesting and the learning outcome was good. The electrochemistry course was not as well taught and the excercises took quite some time to complete and this took time from memorizing the lecture contents.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Be aware that it costs money almost whenever you want some official document so include in your budget money for the papers neede for residence permit, insurance etc. and also for leaving the country again after 5 months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Meat is very expensive and transportations is also quite expensive. The cantine food was very expensive, and most things like reastuarants, clothes, etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sports facilites and offers are exceptional. The music offers are more sparse, and mainly classical.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports of all kinds, classical orchestras, hiking, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetely the intensive language courses and the sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the hills sorrounding Zürich and there are lots of things in the city center. Try the chocolate museum, the Christmas markets, go to Basel and try the ferries on the lake and surfing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Culturally it is very similar to Denmark but people are, if possible, even more reserved than in DK. So try to talk to someone. You have to to the hard work of getting to know people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was not so good at this. There are not a lot of parties or such at uni. Try to approach people in exercise sessions or where you live and try to find people to go to lunch break with. That is a lovely time to get to know, where people meet after lectures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. Even though most people are good at english, they speak swiss german with one another and even if you know some german, this might not be enough to understand swiss german which is very different from german.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything is very organized and people are mostly friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find people to engange with early on. Do not take too many ECTS points. Do sports at ETH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the slides before the lectures and have questions prepared also for the excercise sessions since the time for questions is scarse.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting ither exchange students and experiencing another university and taking courses that are not available at my home university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to follow the high academic pace.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
